fatal_blockers: Proposal 1 recreates the proved pure-power dimension wall. A splitter family that isolates every degree-at-most-r support spans the squarefree message monomials, forcing rank at least sum_{i<=r} binom(k,i); fixed r gives no polynomial-gap amplification, while growing r becomes superpolynomial in the hardness regime.

Proposal 2 does not meet the target reduction: it supplies a direct rational quadratic-form CVP construction, not an explicit binary syndrome instance eligible for O8. Its SDP, normalization, polynomial p, rational factorization, infinite signed-fiber constraint set, and bit-complexity bound are unspecified, while O5 permits constant-support repairs unless their energy is proved large relative to the YES baseline.

Proposal 3 cannot protect every matching with cheap leaders inside one binary affine fiber while charging their odd superpositions. Whenever three legal matchings XOR to an illegal cover, the three corresponding leaders XOR to another target representation of cost at most three times the YES bound; the unspecified address-code search cannot yield a polynomial gap.

Proposal 4 has the same affine-closure failure regardless of whether cup-i or Massey coordinates detect the semantic illegal chain. The linear span contains the XOR of three cheap legal lifts as a cheap target representation, and no higher-operation value attached to the semantic XOR removes that representation; growing-order operations also lack an explicit polynomial-rank binary matrix.

Proposal 6 starts from a false characteristic-two predicate: satisfying-literal sums can cancel, so the clause-product may vanish despite a consistent choice. For example, factors e_x, e_y, and e_x+e_y multiply to zero although x=y=1 is consistent; the full algebra is exponential, while quotient selection and mixed-word soundness are unspecified.

Proposal 5 is the only current opening, but it presently lacks a defined row universe, invariant objective, multiplicity/output-length accounting, and polynomial-time separation algorithm. Exact enumeration of all codewords can itself reveal the nearest witness, so a positive tiny ILP result would remain nonalgorithmic and must not be promoted beyond finite feasibility.
evidence: The pure-power verifier proved dim P_r(D)=sum_{i<=min(k,r)} binom(k,i), independent of coordinate or function-type merging. This directly blocks Proposal 1's claimed coordinate compression from becoming rank compression.

The exchange-quotient verifier found 32 instances where an illegal odd cover lies in the affine span of perfect matchings. That certificate applies directly to Proposals 3 and 4 and to any linear shell assigning cheap representatives to every legal witness.

All-eight and holonomy tests already exhibit illegal mixed words whose nonlinear walk features cancel completely. Any candidate experiment must include both attacks rather than relying on ordinary held-out YES/NO instances.

Existing code-dependent generator-type punctures, sparse hashes, polar shortening, noncommutative folds, condensers, and convolution folds all lost the finite gap; parity-check simplification is rigorously vacuous on the BMT tensor family. These results do not exclude Proposal 5's unrestricted dense row-selection ILP, which is why one bounded feasibility test remains discriminating.

No supplied verifier evaluates Proposal 5's full row-selection optimization over every mixed word. A negative exact optimum would close a materially broader tiny-instance fold class than the previously frozen maps, while a positive result would only justify investigating an efficient surrogate.
next_experiment: Implement only Proposal 5 after freezing a canonical ILP: enumerate all distinct nonzero linear row functionals on each reduced 8-by-8 tensor code, use integer multiplicities with total output length at most 64, specify rank-one completeness and every-mixed-word soundness constraints solely from G, and use relabeling-invariant lexicographic tie-breaking. Solve exactly on precommitted YES, NO, affine-closure, all-eight, and holonomy codes; reject on any pointed kernel, hostile cost at most worst YES, uniform ratio at most 25/9, output length at least 65, or relabeling failure. Report only finite feasibility and runtime/separation complexity, not an asymptotic claim.
